lessonActivities.title: Each Other/One Another/Ourselves – Reciprocal & Reflexive! 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
Welcome to reciprocal and reflexive pronouns! Each other, one another, and ourselves show relationships and self-reference. 🔄

Core Concept: These pronouns show how people relate to each other or themselves.

Three Types:

Information
Reciprocal: Each other/one another (mutual actions)
Reflexive: Ourselves (self-reference)
Usage: Small groups vs large groups vs self

Important Note: Each other = two people, one another = more than two, ourselves = we referring to ourselves.

Common Mistakes: Using wrong pronoun for group size or confusing with possessive.
examples: John and Mary love each other. (two people, mutual)
The students help one another. (group, mutual)
We enjoyed ourselves at the party. (we referring to ourselves)
They talk to each other every day. (reciprocal action)
We prepared ourselves for the exam. (reflexive action)
The team supports one another. (group reciprocity)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Quick Rule: Each other = 2 people. One another = 3+ people. Ourselves = we to ourselves.

lessonActivities.title: Each Other – Reciprocal for Pairs 👫
lessonActivities.content:
Master each other for reciprocal actions between two people. 👫

Each Other Usage:

Information
Two people: John and Mary, he and she
Mutual actions: Both do the same to each other
Two-way: Action goes both directions
Small groups: Sometimes used for small groups

Context Matters: Emphasizes the pair relationship.

Practice Strategy: Think of couples, partners, or best friends.
examples: Tom and Jerry fight each other. (two characters)
The twins look like each other. (mutual resemblance)
My parents love each other. (marital relationship)
The two friends help each other. (mutual help)
They kissed each other. (reciprocal action)
The neighbors visit each other. (mutual visits)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Pair Rule: Each other = exactly two people or things.

lessonActivities.title: One Another – Reciprocal for Groups 👥
lessonActivities.content:
Learn one another for reciprocal actions in larger groups. 👥

One Another Usage:

Information
Three or more: Groups, teams, classes
Formal tone: More formal than 'each other'
Mutual actions: All members interact reciprocally
Group dynamics: Shows group relationships

Regional Note: Americans often prefer 'each other' even for groups.

Advanced Tip: One another sounds more sophisticated.
examples: The students respect one another. (class group)
Team members trust one another. (work team)
The children play with one another. (group of kids)
Colleagues support one another. (office group)
The musicians inspire one another. (band members)
Friends help one another. (group of friends)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Group Rule: One another = three or more people.

lessonActivities.title: Ourselves – Reflexive Pronoun 🔄
lessonActivities.content:
Master ourselves as a reflexive pronoun for self-reference. 🔄

Ourselves Usage:

Information
Reflexive: Subject and object are the same ('we')
Self-actions: We do something to ourselves
Emphasis: We did it ourselves (by ourselves)
Reciprocal: Can show mutual actions within 'we'

Grammar Rule: Must refer back to subject pronoun 'we'.

Use when the subject 'we' is doing something to itself.
examples: We prepared ourselves for the test. (reflexive)
We enjoyed ourselves at the party. (reflexive)
We built the house ourselves. (by ourselves)
We have to defend ourselves. (reflexive)
We taught ourselves English. (self-taught)
We can take care of ourselves. (self-care)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Reflexive Rule: Ourselves refers back to 'we' (subject = object).

lessonActivities.title: Choosing the Right Pronoun – Context Matters ⚖️
lessonActivities.content:
Learn when to choose each other, one another, or ourselves. ⚖️

Decision Guide:

Information
Each other: Two people/things, mutual actions
One another: Three+ people/things, formal mutual actions
Ourselves: 'We' referring to itself, self-actions
Group size: Determines reciprocal pronoun choice

Context Test: Count the people involved to choose correctly.

Identify the subject and see what type of relationship is shown.
examples: John and Mary love each other. (2 people, reciprocal)
The three friends help one another. (3+ people, reciprocal)
We taught ourselves the language. (we → ourselves, reflexive)
The couple hugged each other. (2 people, mutual)
The team supports one another. (group, mutual)
We protected ourselves from the rain. (we → ourselves, self-action)
My parents know each other. (2 people, mutual knowledge)
We blame ourselves for the mistake. (we → ourselves, self-blame)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Choice Rule: Count people: 2 = each other, 3+ = one another, we = ourselves.

lessonActivities.title: Mastering Reciprocal & Reflexive – Natural Usage 🏆
lessonActivities.content:
Put it all together! Use these pronouns naturally in communication. 🏆

Communication Strategies:

Information
Relationships: Each other for pairs, one another for groups
Self-reference: Ourselves for 'we' actions
Emphasis: By ourselves, to ourselves
Reciprocity: Mutual actions and feelings

Advanced Tip: Ourselves can show both reflexive and reciprocal meanings.
examples: The couple understands each other perfectly. (pair relationship)
The colleagues respect one another in the office. (group respect)
We motivated ourselves to finish the project. (self-motivation)
The siblings fight with each other sometimes. (sibling rivalry)
The students learn from one another. (group learning)
We have to look after ourselves now. (self-care)
The partners trust each other completely. (mutual trust)
We talk to ourselves when we're alone. (self-talk)
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Native Choice: Each other is more common than one another in casual speech.

writingActivities.question: Write 5 sentences using 'each other' for pairs (2 people/things).
writingActivities.hint: Use each other when describing mutual actions between exactly two people or things.

writingActivities.question: Write 5 sentences using 'one another' for groups (3+ people).
writingActivities.hint: Use one another when describing mutual actions in groups of three or more.

writingActivities.question: Write 5 sentences using 'ourselves' as reflexive pronoun.
writingActivities.hint: Use ourselves when 'we' is doing something to itself (subject = object).

writingActivities.question: Write sentences contrasting all three pronouns in similar situations.
writingActivities.hint: Show how each pronoun creates different meanings based on context.

writingActivities.question: Correct pronoun mistakes in these sentences.
writingActivities.hint: Fix wrong pronoun choice based on number of people or reflexive vs reciprocal.
sentenceStarters: We blame each other for the mistake.

writingActivities.question: Write a short dialogue (8-10 exchanges) using reciprocal/reflexive pronouns naturally.
writingActivities.hint: Include relationships between pairs, groups, and self-references.

writingActivities.question: Write sentences showing different relationships with appropriate pronouns.
writingActivities.hint: Choose the right pronoun based on whether it's pair, group, or self-reference.

writingActivities.question: Write formal vs informal descriptions using these pronouns.
writingActivities.hint: Use one another for formal situations, each other for casual, ourselves for self-reference.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct pronoun for two people.
gameActivities.hint: Each other is used for reciprocal actions between two people.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct pronoun for a group of people.
gameActivities.hint: One another is used for reciprocal actions in groups.

gameActivities.question: Which pronoun shows self-reference?
gameActivities.hint: Ourselves is reflexive, referring back to 'we'.

gameActivities.question: Choose the pronoun for mutual actions between partners.
gameActivities.hint: Each other is appropriate for pairs, even in professional contexts.

gameActivities.question: Which pronoun cannot be used for self-reference?
gameActivities.sentence: We need to protect ____ from danger.
gameActivities.hint: Only ourselves can be used for reflexive self-reference with 'we'.

quizActivities.question: Which pronoun is used for reciprocal actions between two people?
quizActivities.hint: Each other is for mutual actions between exactly two people.
quizActivities.explanation: Each other shows reciprocal actions between two individuals.

quizActivities.question: Which pronoun is used for reciprocal actions in groups?
quizActivities.hint: One another is for mutual actions among three or more people.
quizActivities.explanation: One another indicates reciprocal relationships in groups.

quizActivities.question: What's the difference between each other and one another?
options: Each other = 2 people, one another = 3+ people
Each other = groups, one another = pairs
Each other is formal, one another is casual
quizActivities.correctAnswer: Each other = 2 people, one another = 3+ people
quizActivities.hint: The number of people determines the choice.
quizActivities.explanation: Each other is for pairs, one another for groups of three or more.

quizActivities.question: Which pronoun is reflexive (subject = object)?
quizActivities.hint: Ourselves refers back to the subject 'we'.
quizActivities.explanation: Ourselves is a reflexive pronoun where subject and object are the same.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence uses the pronouns correctly?
options: The team fights each other constantly.
The couple respects one another deeply.
We blame ourselves for the accident.
The students prepared each other for the exam.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: We blame ourselves for the accident.
quizActivities.hint: Check if the pronoun matches the number of people and type of action.
quizActivities.explanation: We blame ourselves is correct - reflexive pronoun with matching subject.

spellingActivities.hint: Mutual or shared between two or more
spellingActivities.sentence: Each other and one another are ____ pronouns.
